what_they_do: Frontier lab behind the FLUX image models; in July 2026 launched FLUX 3, one model trained jointly on image, video, audio and robot-action prediction. Offices in Freiburg and San Francisco.

signals.signal: $300M Series B at $3.25B post-money (co-led by Salesforce Ventures and AMP; a16z, NVIDIA, General Catalyst, Temasek). Money is earmarked for scaling research, increasing compute capacity and growing teams in Freiburg and SF.
Launched FLUX 3, a multimodal frontier model (image, video, audio, action) trained 'by scaling up compute and data resources'. Faster and open-weight versions are planned for later in 2026.
First robotics/action model (Flux-mimic, built with Swiss startup mimic and validated with Audi Production Lab). This marks the shift to physical AI.

est_gpu_need: 1,000-4,000 H100-equiv for training plus heavy inference. Joint video/audio/action training is far more compute-hungry than image-only FLUX, and video inference for API partners (Canva, Figma, Cloudflare and others) scales with usage.
timing_rationale: FLUX 3 shipped in July 2026. Open-weight and faster variants arrive in late 2026, and the next training cycle (FLUX 3.x, action models) plus video-inference growth lands in Q1-Q2 2027. A German-headquartered lab gains from EU-sited, isolated capacity in 0.5 MW increments.

what_they_do: European defence-AI company that builds AI software, autonomous systems and drones for NATO and allied militaries. It is the most valuable startup in mainland Europe.

signals.signal: $1.8B Series E at an $18B valuation, Europe's largest defence-tech round (Dragoneer, Lightspeed, Goldman Sachs Alternatives, JPMorganChase, CPP Investments, General Catalyst). Proceeds go to developing and integrating advanced AI platforms across partner nations.
Round first reported in May as a $1.2B raise at $18B; demand exceeded the allocation.
Defence News coverage of the record round.

est_gpu_need: 256-1,000 H100-equiv, mostly training. Covers perception, sensor-fusion and autonomy models, large-scale simulation and synthetic data. Classified or national data needs isolated, sovereign-controlled clusters.
timing_rationale: $1.8B was deployed from mid-2026 into multi-country AI platform integration. Defence workloads cannot run on shared clouds, so dedicated liquid-cooled blocks under a client-controlled SPV match the requirement. Capacity planning for H1 2027 programmes is happening now.

segment: European model lab - world models / physical AI
what_they_do: Frontier research lab founded by Yann LeCun to build world models trained on real-world data, for robotics, healthcare and industrial systems. Offices in New York, Montreal and Singapore.

signals.signal: $1.03B seed at a $3.5B pre-money valuation, Europe's largest seed ever. Co-led by Cathay Innovation, Greycroft, Hiro Capital, HV Capital and Bezos Expeditions; NVIDIA and Samsung are strategic investors.
Coverage notes AMI needs GPUs and training capacity before shipping product, and that its strategic investors have a stake in the compute world models will demand.

est_gpu_need: 1,000-4,000+ H100-equiv for training. World models trained on video and sensor data are compute-heavy. With $1B+ raised, likely spend is several hundred million on compute over 2026-2028.
timing_rationale: The lab launched in March 2026 and is in its first major compute ramp. A second wave of cluster procurement for 2027 training runs is likely being negotiated now. Paris headquarters and a European-sovereignty narrative favour EU-sited capacity.

what_they_do: Kyutai spin-out building ultra-low-latency, multilingual real-time voice and audio models for voice agents.

signals.signal: Seed extended to $100M, about seven months after launch, with NVIDIA as a new investor. Opening a Bay Area office.
Launched from stealth with a $70M seed (FirstMark, Eurazeo, DST Global Partners, Eric Schmidt, Xavier Niel).
Lead investor's thesis is titled 'Arming the rebels with GPUs': the company is explicitly compute-centric.

est_gpu_need: 128-512 H100-equiv, split between training and real-time inference. Audio foundation-model training plus latency-sensitive serving; inference grows with voice-agent adoption.
timing_rationale: Fresh capital from July 2026 and NVIDIA backing. The next model generation and production voice-agent traffic should ramp in H1 2027. Real-time voice serving in Europe needs low-latency, EU-resident capacity, which 0.5 MW blocks size well.

segment: AI-native app with own models (language AI)
what_they_do: Language-AI company with translation, writing and agent products. It trains its own LLMs on owned NVIDIA DGX SuperPODs hosted in colocation.

signals.signal: Deployed its third NVIDIA DGX SuperPOD, the first DGX GB200 system in Europe, at EcoDataCenter in Sweden. Shows a repeat pattern of buying dedicated clusters.
CEO discussed laying off about 25% of the workforce and said IPO markets are not open for companies of DeepL's size. Signals cost discipline.
CEO says staying private has 'a lot of advantages' right now.

est_gpu_need: 500-2,000 H100-equiv for training and inference. Past SuperPOD purchases (H100 'Mercury', then GB200) suggest the next refresh is on a similar scale.
timing_rationale: Cluster purchases have come roughly every 18-24 months (2023 H100, mid-2025 GB200), so the next capacity decision falls around H1 2027. After the layoffs, a dedicated cluster bought as opex or through an SPV, rather than owned capex, may appeal. DeepL already uses Nordic colocation.

segment: European model lab - agentic / computer-use models
what_they_do: Builds action-oriented AI agents and its own computer-use models (the Holo family) for enterprise automation.

signals.signal: Released Holo 3, its latest generation of computer-use models (exact 2026 date not verified).
Record $220M seed (Bpifrance, Eurazeo, Xavier Niel and others), part of the background for continued model training.

est_gpu_need: 256-1,000 H100-equiv for training (RL on UI environments) and agent inference. Computer-use agents consume many tokens per task, so enterprise rollout drives inference.
timing_rationale: Holo 3 is in market in 2026, so the next model generation and enterprise agent serving will need capacity in H1 2027. A follow-on raise is probable given seed-era capital. French sovereign positioning suits EU-resident, isolated capacity.

what_they_do: Software-defined autonomous air, land and sea systems (for example the Vector ISR drone) that combine unmanned platforms with AI, sensors and mission-control software.

Coverage of the Series D to accelerate multi-domain autonomy.

est_gpu_need: 128-512 H100-equiv for training. Covers perception and autonomy models, sensor fusion, simulation and synthetic data for multi-domain platforms. Defence data argues for isolated clusters.
timing_rationale: Capital from July 2026 is going into scaling and acquisitions. The jump to multi-domain autonomy needs more training capacity during 2027, and sovereign or defence data needs dedicated, client-controlled infrastructure.

hq_city: Berlin (dual HQ with Toronto); Heidelberg research centre
what_they_do: Enterprise LLM company. Once combined with Aleph Alpha it will operate as Cohere, positioned as a sovereign alternative to US AI for European governments and enterprises.

Definitive combination agreement: Berlin/Toronto dual HQ, growing past 1,000 employees across Canada and Germany, with government backing for sovereign AI.
TechCrunch analysis of why the companies are merging.

est_gpu_need: 1,000-4,000 H100-equiv for sovereign training and inference in Germany/EU. Sovereign enterprise and government customers need in-country, isolated serving and fine-tuning.
timing_rationale: The merger signed in September 2026, so integration and a German sovereign-capacity build-out fall in H1 2027. Risk: Schwarz (STACKIT) is an investor and may be the default supplier. Pitch overflow or SPV-isolated capacity for specific government customers.

segment: AI for science / pharma (enterprise sovereign AI)

Coverage of the 3,500-GPU deployment across hybrid cloud and on-prem.

Coverage of the Series A to expand the autonomous heavy-equipment platform.

Named among European robotics startups building foundation models in a period of record robotics funding (H1 2026).

segment: European model lab (stretch account; also sells compute)
what_they_do: Europe's leading frontier LLM developer. Building its own data centres and also selling 'Mistral AI Cloud' capacity, so it is partly a competitor.

signals.signal: Raised EUR3B led by Samsung at a valuation above EUR21B, the largest European tech round.
$830M debt to complete a 44 MW data centre at Bruyères-le-Châtel with 13,800 GB300 GPUs (operational from Q2 2026).
Targets 200 MW of compute across European sites by end-2027 and 1 GW by 2030.
1.4 GW Paris campus joint venture with MGX, Bpifrance and NVIDIA; construction H2 2026, operations 2028.

est_gpu_need: Gigawatt-scale self-build. The only realistic opening is bridging capacity: going from 44 MW today to a 200 MW target by end-2027 could need 5-10 MW (2,500-4,000 GPUs) of interim dedicated capacity.
timing_rationale: The gap between 44 MW live and the 200 MW end-2027 target, with the 1.4 GW campus not live until 2028, could create interim demand in H1 2027. Low probability: Mistral builds its own and also resells compute.
